messages:
alex: FYI i ran a focused long-context sweep on delta7b int8 vs fp16. economics look great but quality regressions on multi-paragraph summaries popped up. putting raw numbers here and a couple rollout options.
marta: thanks alex, drop the numbers and sample notes please.
alex: summary (slice=multi-par-summ, avg input ~950 tokens, N=720):
```
- p95 latency: fp16 195ms | int8 235ms
- throughput (tokens/sec): fp16 0.98 | int8 0.42
- cost per 1k tokens: fp16 $0.0080 | int8 $0.0035
- automated recall@5 (gold): fp16 78.1% | int8 72.9%  (delta -5.2pp)
- ROUGE-L mean drop: 4.2 pts
- hallucination heuristic rate: fp16 2.1% | int8 5.6%
- note: failure modes concentrated when prompt includes multi-document citations + long system priming
```
link: https://internal.redwood/sparkbench/delta7b/3100001111
ryan: econ lens: ~2.3-2.4x token cost reduction. For services heavy on long summaries that could translate to ~35-45% cost savings overall if we migrate, but the quality delta looks material for retention workflows. need sensitivity curve for churn vs recall.
devin: initial mitigation ideas: 1) length-based routing, 2) novelty/coverage score threshold, 3) aggressive KV/prefix caching for long contexts to reduce fp16 spend. hybrid rule example below.
```
# routing pseudocode
if request.tokens >= 768 or doc_coverage_score < 0.55:
    route -> delta7b-fp16
elif request.tokens < 128:
    route -> delta7b-int8
else:
    route -> delta7b-int8 with monitor
```
marta: product note: long multi-doc summaries are ~9% of traffic but ~40% of onboarding/enterprise retention paths. small percent but high impact.
ryan: recommended experiment: 3% canary where int8 is default but for the long-doc slice we force route to fp16 for 10% of those requests (i.e., observe both in parallel). collect both live quality signals + offline golden evals.
devin: caching note: our prior KVCACHE config reduced fp16 cost on long contexts by ~30% (same quality). combining caching + routing could make fp16 less expensive and tilt the econ. also we could try mixed-precision fallback only on tokens after 512 (i.e., chunked decoding).
alex: proposed rollout + auto-fallback policy:
1) launch 72h canary: int8 default globally, long-doc slice route 10% -> fp16, collect metrics
2) signal collection: rouge, recall@5, hallucination heuristic, user-report rate
3) auto-fallback: if delta(rouge|recall) > 3.0 pts for 4h on canary -> route_all_long_docs -> fp16 & page #eng-ml + #product
4) manual review window 24h before broader roll

fallback pseudocode:
```
monitor_window = 4h
if recall_delta(fp16,int8) > 3.0 pts over monitor_window:
    set_routing(long_docs, target="fp16")
    trigger_alert(channels=["#eng-ml", "#product"])
```
ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary created: delta7b-int8-global w/ long-doc 10% fp16 probe. See https://internal.redwood/deploys/3100001111
marta: sounds good. ryan can you add a slide with cost curve + churn sensitivity? devin can you draft KVCACHE config and an ops playbook snippet? i'll coordinate with GTN on user-impact assumptions.
ryan: on it. i'll model churn impact assuming 1pt recall loss -> 0.5% retention drop and push likely/unlikely scenarios.
devin: i'll stub a caching config and include a recommended quant ladder (int8 short, fp16 long, try int6 microbench later) in the playbook.
alex: i'll start the 72h collection and post interim numbers in this thread. ping if you want early logs. :rocket:
